title: US 2.0: Not at the Dinner Table

sentences.en: Today's show is brought to you by T-Mobile for Business.
sentences.zh: 今天的节目由 T-Mobile for Business 赞助播出。

sentences.en: We typically divide the United States into two political categories.
sentences.zh: 我们通常将美国分为两个政治阵营。

sentences.en: Democrats have blocked us at every turn.
sentences.zh: 民主党人在每一个环节都阻挠我们。

sentences.en: Finding common ground between these two groups.
sentences.zh: 在这两个群体之间寻找共同点。
他们那些极端的激进派基础。

sentences.en: Because we keep trying to find a way to win without help from across the aisle.
sentences.zh: 因为我们一直在试图寻找一种无需对方阵营帮助就能获胜的方法。

sentences.en: This is true not just in a metaphorical sense.
sentences.zh: 这不仅仅是在隐喻意义上是真实的。

sentences.en: In one study, researchers looked at more than 1,400 hours of tape on C-SPAN.
sentences.zh: 在一项研究中，研究人员查看了 C-SPAN 上超过 1400 小时的录像。

sentences.en: The clerk will call the roll.
After all these hours watching C-SPAN, researchers concluded that since the 1990s, Democrats and Republicans in the U.S.
sentences.zh: 在观看了这么多小时的 C-SPAN 后，研究人员得出结论：自 20 世纪 90 年代以来，美国的民主党人和共和党人

sentences.en: Senate have physically crossed the aisle less and less to interact with opposing colleagues.
sentences.zh: 在参议院里，他们跨越党派界线与对方同事互动的次数越来越少。

sentences.en: That means senators are staying with their like-minded colleagues, not just in the legislation they are trying to pass,
sentences.zh: 这意味着参议员们不仅在试图通过的立法上与志同道合的同事待在一起，

sentences.en: but also by literally steering clear of the carpeted pathway that splits the Senate floor.
sentences.zh: 而且在物理空间上也刻意避开那条分割参议院大厅的铺设地毯的通道。

sentences.en: Today, we continue our Us 2.0 series by taking a few steps back and looking at the challenge of political division through a new lens.
sentences.zh: 今天，我们继续“我们 2.0”系列节目，退后几步，通过一个新的视角审视政治分歧带来的挑战。

sentences.en: We hope we will provide a new way to understand the people sitting across from us at the dinner table.
sentences.zh: 我们希望提供一种新的方式来理解坐在餐桌对面的人。

sentences.en: People don't seem to dislike somebody just for being a member of the other side.
sentences.zh: 人们似乎并不只是因为对方是另一阵营的成员而讨厌他们。

sentences.en: They're concerned that somebody is going to talk to them about politics.
sentences.zh: 他们担心的是对方会找他们谈论政治。

sentences.en: And if somebody is going to talk to you about politics, of course you'd rather talk to somebody of your own side.
sentences.zh: 如果有人要跟你谈论政治，你当然更愿意和自己阵营的人谈。

sentences.en: This week on Hidden Brain, why the division you hear about all the time in our politics might not be what really divides us.
sentences.zh: 本周的《Hidden Brain》，探讨为什么我们政治中一直听到的那种分歧，可能并非真正分裂我们的原因。

sentences.en: Yana Krupnikov is a political scientist at the University of Michigan.
sentences.zh: Yana Krupnikov 是密歇根大学的一位政治学家。

sentences.en: She studies a subject we hear about a lot, the bitter political divide in the United States.
sentences.zh: 她研究的是我们经常听到的一个话题：美国国内激烈的政治分歧。

sentences.en: But Yana has a counterintuitive thesis.
sentences.zh: 但 Yana 有一个反直觉的论点。

sentences.en: She thinks the real fault line in America is actually not between Republicans and Democrats.
sentences.zh: 她认为美国真正的分歧点其实并不在于共和党人和民主党人之间。

sentences.en: Yana Krupnikov, welcome to Hidden Brain.
I want to play you a clip, Yana, from a CNN program titled, Welcome to the Fractured States of America.
sentences.zh: Yana，我想给你放一段 CNN 节目的片段，标题是《欢迎来到分裂的美国》。

sentences.en: The number of parents who would be unhappy if their child married someone of a different political party,
sentences.zh: 如果子女与不同政党的人结婚，父母会感到不高兴，这一比例

sentences.en: that number has exploded over the last several decades, from 4% in 1960 to 35% of Republicans and 45% of Democrats in 2018.
sentences.zh: 在过去几十年里急剧上升，从 1960 年的 4% 上升到 2018 年共和党人的 35% 和民主党人的 45%。

sentences.en: Yana, you have a critique of this notion of a fractured country, but I want you to start by laying out the conventional wisdom firSt.
sentences.zh: Yana，你对这种“国家分裂”的观点有批评意见，但我希望你先阐述一下传统观点。

sentences.en: What are we all told about the state of political polarization in the United States?
sentences.zh: 关于美国政治极化的现状，我们都被告知了些什么？

sentences.en: A lot of what we're told about the state of political polarization is that polarization has increased quite vastly over potentially the last decade.
sentences.zh: 关于政治极化现状，我们被告知的很多内容是，极化在过去十年里可能已经大幅加剧。

sentences.en: What's interesting about this polarization is that there's a twofold approach here.
sentences.zh: 这种极化有趣的地方在于，它有两种表现方式。

sentences.en: So on the one hand, polarization can be ideological, but on the other hand, it can be affective.
sentences.zh: 一方面，极化可以是意识形态上的，但另一方面，它也可以是情感上的。

sentences.en: And affective polarization is the sense of disliking somebody just because they're a member of the other party,
sentences.zh: 而情感极化是指仅仅因为对方是另一政党的成员就讨厌某人，

sentences.en: without their issues, without kind of their positions, just because they belong to this opposing group.
sentences.zh: 不考虑他们的议题，不考虑他们的立场，仅仅因为他们属于那个对立群体。

sentences.en: So when we talk about Democrats not wanting their child to marry a Republican,
sentences.zh: 所以当我们谈论民主党人不想让他们的孩子嫁给共和党人时，

sentences.en: or Republicans not wanting their child to marry a Democrat, we're talking often about this idea of affect,
sentences.zh: 或者共和党人不想让他们的孩子嫁给民主党人时，我们通常谈论的是这种情感上的观念，

sentences.en: just this sense of dislike, this antipathy for the other side.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是一种厌恶感，一种对另一方的反感。

sentences.en: And there's this tremendous kind of pattern showing increases in this level of antipathy,
sentences.zh: 而且有一种巨大的模式显示这种反感程度在增加，

sentences.en: that people who are from one party just dislike the other party much more than they did in years paSt.
sentences.zh: 即来自一个政党的人比过去几年更讨厌另一个政党。

sentences.en: And some of this is almost to an extreme.
sentences.zh: 其中一些甚至达到了极端的程度。

sentences.en: I mean, some people have even asked whether ordinary Americans see their political opponents as even fully human.
sentences.zh: 我是说，有些人甚至问过，普通美国人是否还把他们的政治对手视为完整的人。

sentences.en: There's actually a lot of examples of this antipathy.
sentences.zh: 实际上有很多这种反感的例子。

sentences.en: There's research suggesting that people wouldn't want somebody to, as I just said, marry somebody from the other party,
sentences.zh: 有研究表明，人们不想让某人，正如我刚才所说，与另一政党的人结婚，

sentences.en: that they wouldn't want to hire somebody from the opposing party,
sentences.zh: 他们不想雇佣来自对立政党的人，

sentences.en: that they don't see the other party as human, that they might actually want to do something
sentences.zh: 他们不把对方政党的人视为人类，他们甚至可能真的想做些什么

sentences.en: that would make life for somebody from the opposing party much worse.
sentences.zh: 让对立政党的人生活得更糟糕。

sentences.en: So there are a lot of these almost non-political examples of places where partisanship and dislike for the other side
sentences.zh: 所以有很多这种几乎非政治的例子，党派偏见和对另一方的厌恶

sentences.en: has quite profoundly affected the way we see the world and the way we see other people.
sentences.zh: 已经深刻地影响了我们看待世界和看待他人的方式。

sentences.en: So we're told Americans don't want to live next to one another, political partisans, that is.
sentences.zh: 所以我们被告知，美国人不想住在一起，我是指政治党派人士。

sentences.en: They can't bear to talk to one another, and, of course, they don't want their children marrying people from the other party.
sentences.zh: 他们无法忍受与对方交谈，当然，他们也不希望自己的孩子与另一政党的人结婚。

sentences.en: You conducted a survey some years ago when you drilled down specifically on the marriage question.
sentences.zh: 你几年前进行了一项调查，专门深入研究了婚姻问题。

sentences.en: What was the hunch you were exploring, and what did you ask?
sentences.zh: 你当时在探索什么直觉，又问了什么问题？

sentences.en: So the way we looked at the marriage question happened during these conversations I'd had with my co-authors,
sentences.zh: 我们看待婚姻问题的方式源于我与合著者进行的对话，

sentences.en: John Barry Ryan and Samara Clar.
sentences.zh: John Barry Ryan 和 Samara Clar。

sentences.en: And so we were talking about this marriage question that something about it seemed quite unusual to us.
sentences.zh: 我们当时在讨论这个婚姻问题，觉得它有些地方很不寻常。

sentences.en: You're in a survey, you're being asked whether you want your child to marry somebody from the other party,
sentences.zh: 你在参与一项调查，被问及是否希望你的孩子与另一政党的人结婚，

sentences.en: but that's really all you know about this person.
sentences.zh: 但关于这个人，你真正知道的也就只有这些。

sentences.en: All you know about them is that they are a Republican or that they are a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 你对他们唯一的了解就是他们是共和党人或民主党人。

sentences.en: And when that's all you know about them, one, you can't really put that person into context.
sentences.zh: 而当你对他们唯一的了解仅限于此，第一，你无法真正将那个人置于背景中去理解。

sentences.en: But the other thing you might think about them is essentially, if they're telling me this person's partisanship,
sentences.zh: 但你可能还会想到另一件事，本质上，如果他们告诉我这个人的党派倾向，

sentences.en: that person's partisanship is probably something that's really, really important to them.
sentences.zh: 那么这个人的党派倾向可能对他们来说是非常、非常重要的。

sentences.en: So if I was inviting you to meet one of my friends, and we had just a brief moment,
sentences.zh: 所以如果我邀请你见我的一个朋友，而我们只有很短的时间，

sentences.en: and I used that brief moment to tell you, you're going to meet my friend, she likes cats,
sentences.zh: 我利用那短暂的时间告诉你，你要见我的朋友，她喜欢猫，

sentences.en: you might imagine that you're about to meet somebody who is essentially going to talk nonstop about cats.
sentences.zh: 你可能会想象你即将见到的人会不停地谈论猫。

sentences.en: That's the only thing I shared with you about this person.
sentences.zh: 那是我关于这个人分享给你的唯一信息。

sentences.en: And so what if this is what's happening in a survey?
sentences.zh: 那么，如果调查中发生的情况也是这样呢？

sentences.en: What if when people are asked about this hypothetical in-law,
sentences.zh: 如果当人们被问及这个假设的姻亲时，

sentences.en: and the only thing they know about this person is that they're a member of the opposing party?
sentences.zh: 而他们对这个人唯一的了解就是对方是反对党的成员？

sentences.en: What if they're imagining somebody who will literally talk about politics
sentences.zh: 如果他们想象的是一个会从今往后的每一顿晚餐都谈论政治的人，

sentences.en: for every dinner from now on as their in-law?
And what did you find when you actually asked Americans this question?
sentences.zh: 当你真正问美国人这个问题时，你发现了什么？

sentences.en: How did you tweak the question?
sentences.zh: 你是如何调整这个问题的？

sentences.en: So what we ended up doing is we amended the question a bit.
sentences.zh: 我们最终做的是对问题进行了一些修正。
我们基本上增加了一个限定条件。

sentences.en: We told people that this future in-law, this hypothetical in-law,
sentences.zh: 我们告诉人们，这个未来的姻亲，这个假设的姻亲，

sentences.en: was actually never really going to talk about politics.
sentences.zh: 实际上永远不会谈论政治。

sentences.en: They might be from the other parties, but they were never actually going to discuss anything political.
sentences.zh: 他们可能来自其他政党，但他们实际上永远不会讨论任何政治话题。

sentences.en: And so we ran an experiment in which people were randomly assigned to either a group in which
sentences.zh: 所以我们进行了一项实验，人们被随机分配到两组中，其中一组

sentences.en: they got asked the normal question,
how happy would you be if your child married somebody from the opposing party?
sentences.zh: 如果你的孩子与来自对立政党的人结婚，你会多高兴？

sentences.en: Versus a question in which they were told,
sentences.zh: 而另一组则被问及一个问题，其中他们被告知，

sentences.en: how happy would you be if your child married somebody from an opposing party,
sentences.zh: 如果你的孩子与来自对立政党的人结婚，你会多高兴，

sentences.en: but this person was never going to talk about politics?
sentences.zh: 但这个人永远不会谈论政治？

sentences.en: And what we found is significant differences in people's preferences for the other side.
sentences.zh: 我们发现人们对另一方的偏好存在显著差异。

sentences.en: Once people were told that their child's future spouse was actually not really going to talk about politics,
sentences.zh: 一旦人们被告知他们孩子未来的配偶实际上不会谈论政治，

sentences.en: their animosity toward the other side quite profoundly decreased.
sentences.zh: 他们对另一方的敌意就大大降低了。

sentences.en: In other words, if I was a Republican parent,
sentences.zh: 换句话说，如果我是一位共和党父母，

sentences.en: the thing that I might be most worried about is not that my child is going to marry a Democrat.
sentences.zh: 我最担心的可能不是我的孩子要嫁给一个民主党人。

sentences.en: My child is going to marry a Democrat who's going to talk politics all the time.
sentences.zh: 而是我的孩子要嫁给一个会一直谈论政治的民主党人。

sentences.en: If I had the reassurance that politics was not going to come up all the time,
sentences.zh: 如果我得到保证说政治话题不会一直出现，

sentences.en: my feelings about my future Democratic son-in-law or daughter-in-law changed quite profoundly.
sentences.zh: 我对未来民主党女婿或儿媳的感受就会发生深刻的变化。

sentences.en: In theory, what people were concerned about is essentially politics coming up in their day-to-day lives.
sentences.zh: 理论上，人们担心的是政治出现在他们的日常生活中。

sentences.en: They actually were not as concerned about the opposing partisanship component of it.
sentences.zh: 他们实际上并不那么担心对方的党派成分。

sentences.en: To better understand how this played out in people's lives,
sentences.zh: 为了更好地理解这一点在人们生活中是如何体现的，

sentences.en: Yana and her colleagues ran the study again,
sentences.zh: Yana 和她的同事再次进行了这项研究，

sentences.en: but changed whether the hypothetical new daughter or son-in-law
sentences.zh: 但改变了假设的新儿媳或女婿

sentences.en: talked about politics frequently, occasionally, or rarely.
sentences.zh: 谈论政治的频率：经常、偶尔还是很少。

sentences.en: They found that what people cared about the most
sentences.zh: 他们发现人们最在意的

sentences.en: was not whether a future son-in-law or daughter-in-law had different politics,
sentences.zh: 不是未来的女婿或儿媳是否有不同的政治立场，

sentences.en: but how much the future in-law wanted to talk about politics.
sentences.zh: 而是未来的姻亲有多想谈论政治。

sentences.en: People don't seem to dislike somebody just for being a member of the other side.
sentences.zh: 人们似乎并不只是因为对方是另一阵营的成员而讨厌他们。

sentences.en: They're concerned that somebody is going to talk to them about politics.
sentences.zh: 他们担心的是对方会找他们谈论政治。

sentences.en: And if somebody is going to talk to you about politics,
sentences.zh: 如果有人要跟你谈论政治，

sentences.en: of course you'd rather talk to somebody of your own side.
sentences.zh: 你当然更愿意和自己阵营的人谈。

sentences.en: If that's going to be part of your life at every dinner,
sentences.zh: 如果这会成为你每一顿晚餐生活的一部分，

sentences.en: certainly, of course, you wouldn't want it to be contentious.
sentences.zh: 当然，你肯定不希望它是充满争议的。

sentences.en: But the key aspect there is conversations, not necessarily partisanship.
sentences.zh: 但其中的关键点是对话，而不一定是党派偏见。

sentences.en: So I'm thinking of a clip from Saturday Night Live that I think your research speaks to.
sentences.zh: 所以我想到《周六夜现场》的一个片段，我认为你的研究可以解释它。

sentences.en: It's actually about a wedding celebration,
sentences.zh: 那其实是关于一场婚礼庆典，

sentences.en: and the celebration is interrupted by the character known as Debbie Downer.
sentences.zh: 庆典被一个叫“Debbie Downer”的角色打断了。

sentences.en: Yeah, these mashed potatoes look like heaven.
sentences.zh: 是啊，这些土豆泥看起来简直太棒了。

sentences.en: After we eat, I vote we get a line dance call.
sentences.zh: 吃完饭后，我提议我们来跳排舞。

sentences.en: Hey, speaking of voting, how do you guys feel about Trump?
sentences.zh: 嘿，说到投票，你们觉得特朗普怎么样？

sentences.en: Do you think that clip speaks to your thesis?
sentences.zh: 你认为那个片段能印证你的论点吗？

sentences.en: I think it speaks to the thesis quite profoundly.
sentences.zh: 我认为它非常深刻地印证了这一论点。

sentences.en: I think actually that is exactly what people are quite worried about.
sentences.zh: 我实际上认为这正是人们非常担心的。

sentences.en: You're having kind of a nice celebration.
sentences.zh: 你正在享受一场美好的庆典。

sentences.en: Somebody comes in for whom politics is incredibly important,
sentences.zh: 有人进来了，对他们来说政治极其重要，

sentences.en: who is essentially going to change the conversation to that particular bent.
sentences.zh: 他们本质上会把谈话转向那个特定的方向。

sentences.en: So imagine that every dinner, you're now incredibly tense,
sentences.zh: 所以想象一下，每一顿晚餐，你现在都感到极其紧张，

sentences.en: trying to figure out, is there something political that's going to happen here?
sentences.zh: 试图弄清楚，这里会不会发生什么政治话题？

sentences.en: I think that's what people are deeply concerned about.
sentences.zh: 我认为这就是人们深感担忧的地方。

sentences.en: Imagine sitting at dinner with friends and family.
sentences.zh: 想象一下和朋友家人坐在一起吃晚餐。

sentences.en: Someone mentions a tweet from Trump.
sentences.zh: 有人提到了特朗普的一条推文。

sentences.en: Yana's data suggests that if the people around your table were a cross-section of America,
sentences.zh: Yana 的数据表明，如果坐在你桌边的人是美国社会的缩影，

sentences.en: most would prefer to change the topic.
sentences.zh: 大多数人会更愿意转换话题。

sentences.en: But some people would get super excited.
sentences.zh: 但有些人会变得非常兴奋。

sentences.en: It's these people who would also be really upset
sentences.zh: 正是这些人，如果他们的孩子要与另一政党的人结婚，

sentences.en: if a child of theirs were to marry someone from the other party.
sentences.zh: 他们也会感到非常不安。

sentences.en: There certainly is a group of people who are, in fact, effectively polarized.
sentences.zh: 确实有一群人，他们实际上是情感极化的。

sentences.en: No matter how we describe this in-law,
sentences.zh: 无论我们如何描述这位姻亲，

sentences.en: they are displeased with their child marrying somebody of the opposing side.
sentences.zh: 他们都不乐意看到自己的孩子与对立阵营的人结婚。

sentences.en: I would bet that even if we told them
sentences.zh: 我敢打赌，即使我们告诉他们

sentences.en: politics will literally never come up ever, ever, ever,
sentences.zh: 政治话题绝对、绝对、绝对不会出现，

sentences.en: they would still be displeased that their child married somebody of the opposing party.
sentences.zh: 他们依然会因为孩子与对立党派的人结婚而不悦。

sentences.en: These people struck us as being what we would term unconditionally polarized.
sentences.zh: 这些人给我们的印象是我们可以称之为“无条件极化”的人。

sentences.en: They were sort of polarized exactly in the sense of hating somebody just because they are from the other side.
sentences.zh: 他们那种极化，恰恰就是因为对方来自对立阵营而讨厌对方。

sentences.en: And as we dove into this question further,
sentences.zh: 随着我们进一步深入研究这个问题，

sentences.en: we wanted to investigate exactly what contributes to this unconditional polarization,
sentences.zh: 我们想调查清楚到底是什么导致了这种无条件的极化，

sentences.en: what correlates with somebody disliking somebody just from being a member of the other side,
sentences.zh: 是什么因素与一个人仅仅因为对方是另一阵营的成员就厌恶对方有关，

sentences.en: which led us to this idea of certain people being deeply involved in politics,
sentences.zh: 这引导我们得出了一个观点，即某些人深度卷入了政治，

sentences.en: people for whom politics has become so profoundly important
sentences.zh: 对这些人来说，政治已经变得如此重要，

sentences.en: that it is something beyond just an interest in politics.
